CONF01-SESSION-V1.does: boots four panels on four symbols at four timeframes with indicators and orders, and grades CONF-01 compliance from the product's own state
CONF01-SESSION-V1.why_it_is_not_a_self_report: indicators are counted from chart.indicators.active per panel, orders from orderService, and playback from the CONTINUOUS PLAYHEAD (replaySystem.replayTimestamp) rather than the isPlaying flag. A 1h panel at 60x closes a bar once a minute, so a bar-index test cannot tell a slow panel from a stalled one.
CONF01-SESSION-V1.refuses: any run whose four requirements are not all met is labelled DIAGNOSTIC ONLY and carries no acceptance weight

DURATION-TREND-V1.does: least-squares slope per series with a 95% confidence interval on the slope
DURATION-TREND-V1.four_verdicts: CLIMBS / FALLS / BOUNDED / INDETERMINATE. A CI that straddles the flat band is INDETERMINATE, which is NOT a GREEN - that is the distinction DUR-01 asks for and the one this campaign kept missing by reading endpoints.
DURATION-TREND-V1.flat_bands_from: measured noise floors: W88 fresh-load spread 0.73 MB, W90 process census ~10 MB between identical reads, W91b post-GC node stability 1.3%

CONF01-DURATION-GATE-V1.replaces: SINGLE-PAIR-SOAK-V1 as freeze gate (retired per dispatch; same-pair carries no acceptance weight)
CONF01-DURATION-GATE-V1.samples: live heap, heap after two forced collections, DOM counters, elements across frames, per-process OS footprint, per-process CPU from cpuTime deltas, resident bars, _panelFullRawData length, orders, in-flight requests

idle_to_playing.meaning: the ruling's central number reproduced on my own instrument: TradeZella's heap FALLS when it plays (133 -> 104 MB), ours climbs. +152.8 MB live, and +33.0 MB survives a forced collection, so it is not only garbage awaiting a sweep.

against_the_PO.reading: same shape, same GPU cost (47.2 vs 51), CPU comparable. Memory lower because his session holds more history: my panels hold 2,280/1,596/1,911/495 bars. The gap is bar residency, not instrument scope - this is the cross-frame gauge from W88.

C4_cpu_split_under_CONF01.raster: no raster worker threads appear in the trace at all, idle or playing - the same result as W91 at same-pair. The off-thread majority is not raster.
C4_cpu_split_under_CONF01.trace_coverage_caveat: traced renderer threads sum to 60.3% against a process-level 127.5%, so 47% of renderer CPU is captured. Traced GPU threads sum to 15.6% against 47.2%, so 33% of GPU CPU is captured. Every role figure above is a floor, and the process-level figures are the ground truth.
C4_cpu_split_under_CONF01.gpu_47_percent_partial_answer: GPU CPU goes 5.2% idle -> 47.2% playing with the same canvases and the same layout, so ~42 points are playback repaint, not surface count. Naming the remaining two thirds needs a GPU-side trace, which is queued behind the duration gate to avoid contention.

DEFECT_1_replay_speed_setting_is_not_hon.product_arithmetic: chart.js:24826 - rawCandlesPerSecond = replaySystem.speed / timeframeSeconds. At speed 60 on a 1m chart that is 1.0 bars/second.

measured.simulatedSecondsPerWallSecond: 440 to 1070 across runs, i.e. 440x-1070x real time while 60x was selected

DEFECT_1_replay_speed_setting_is_not_hon.controllability_test: setting replaySystem.speed to 6 (ten times slower) moved the rate from 8.24 to 7.41 bars/s, not to 0.82. speedIsControllable = false.
DEFECT_1_replay_speed_setting_is_not_hon.mechanism: the advance is frame-driven, not clock-driven: 10.753 bars/s against 14.86 animation frames/s is 0.724 bars per frame. Rate therefore tracks the frame budget and ignores the selector.
consequences: every CPU, allocation and heap-churn figure this campaign has published at '60x' was taken at roughly ten times that rate, mine included
cross-product CPU comparisons at a nominal 60x are not like-for-like unless the competitor's playback is also frame-bound
it is user-facing: the speed selector does not control speed
DEFECT_1_replay_speed_setting_is_not_hon.owner: A (chart.js replay advance), and it needs a kill-switched fix per KILL-01

DEFECT_2_peer_panels_close_no_bars_in_th.measured: at four symbols, the three peer panels advanced 0 bars/second against expected 0.2 (5m), 0.067 (15m) and 0.017 (1h), across every run, while their playhead advanced at the same 440-1070x as the host. They sit at the last bar of their resident window (idx == bars-1) within about two minutes of arming.
DEFECT_2_peer_panels_close_no_bars_in_th.mechanism_matches_the_ruling: the sixteen _multichartSamePairAsHost guards disable same-pair replay catch-up, so a peer must fetch its own /bars during play. It does not, so it exhausts its window and stops producing bars while continuing to consume a playhead.
DEFECT_2_peer_panels_close_no_bars_in_th.consequence: the shipping configuration does not merely cost more than same-pair; three of four panels stop producing bars. Any four-symbol performance number - including my reference row - is measured with one panel producing and three coasting, so it is a FLOOR on the real cost.
DEFECT_2_peer_panels_close_no_bars_in_th.harness_accommodation: keepConf01Playing re-seeks a panel that has reached the end of its data back to 20% and counts the re-seeks per sample, so the duration gate can hold a live workload. The count is published, because a workload that needs re-seeding to stay alive is evidence about the product.
DEFECT_2_peer_panels_close_no_bars_in_th.owner: A with B (per-panel /bars during play is B's C2 network question)
